config.title: Input validation & data integrity

intro.title: Input validation & data integrity
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web form that securely validates user input before processing it. You will learn the core concept of input validation, which ensures only correct and safe data enters your application to maintain data integrity. The main technologies involved are HTML for the form structure and JavaScript for writing validation logic. By the end, you'll understand how to prevent common security issues by checking and sanitizing user inputs.
intro.usecase: Input validation and data integrity are foundational to secure user interactions across all web applications. For example, a sign-up form must validate email formats and password strength before submission, while an e-commerce checkout must sanitize payment details to prevent injection attacks. In admin dashboards, validation ensures that data filters and configuration panels accept only expected values, maintaining system stability. Every text field, file upload, and API request is a point where robust validation protects both the user's data and the application's backend.

objectives: Implement validation rules for user input fields
Apply sanitization techniques to prevent data corruption
Construct error messages that guide users toward valid input
Configure input constraints to enforce data integrity
Update form state based on validation results
Bind validation logic to form submission events
Render visual feedback for valid and invalid input states

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react' to enable component state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main ValidationForm component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ValidationForm that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name ValidationForm and have it return an empty fragment.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ValidationForm component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component named ValidationForm is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: The component ValidationForm is defined and returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named exactly 'ValidationForm' and returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Ensure you define a function named ValidationForm that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize form state with user input fields
steps.instruction: Inside the ValidationForm component, use useState to create a state object with fields for username, email, and password, all initialized as empty strings.
steps.hint: You'll need to destructure the state variable and setter function from useState. Initialize the state with an object containing empty string values for each field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with multiple fields
const [formData, setFormData] = useState({ name: '', age: '' });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state object that can track user input for validation purposes.
successCriteria: State is initialized with an object containing username, email, and password fields, all set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're initializing all three fields (username, email, password) as empty strings in the state object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to use useState to create a state object with username, email, and password fields, all initialized as empty strings.

steps.title: Initialize validation errors state
steps.instruction: Inside your ValidationForm component, use useState to create a state variable called 'errors' that tracks validation error messages. Initialize it as an object with empty strings for 'username' and 'email' fields.
steps.hint: Create a new state variable similar to your form state, but with error messages instead of user input values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: error state for a form
const [errors, setErrors] = useState({ name: '', age: '' });
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a state variable 'errors' that can store validation error messages for each form field.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable named 'errors' initialized as an object with 'username' and 'email' properties set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your errors state is an object with both 'username' and 'email' properties initialized to empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The errors state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState with an object containing 'username' and 'email' properties set to empty strings.

steps.title: Create input change handler
steps.instruction: Define a handleInputChange function inside your ValidationForm component that updates the formData state when input values change. The function should accept an event parameter and use setFormData to update the corresponding field.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes an event, extracts the input's name and value, and updates formData using the previous state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInputChange function is defined inside the component, ready to be connected to input fields.
successCriteria: The handleInputChange function is defined, accepts an event parameter, and updates formData using setFormData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the handler, but make sure it accepts an event parameter and uses setFormData to update the corresponding field in formData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInputChange function isn't defined correctly. It should accept an event, extract name and value, and update formData using setFormData.

steps.title: Create validation helper functions
steps.instruction: Inside your ValidationForm component, create three validation helper functions: validateUsername, validateEmail, and validatePassword. Each function should take a string parameter and return a boolean indicating whether the input is valid.
steps.hint: Define each function with a parameter (like 'value') and write validation logic inside. For now, you can return 'true' for all functions to make them compile.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three validation functions (validateUsername, validateEmail, validatePassword) are defined inside the component, each accepting a string and returning a boolean.
successCriteria: The component contains validateUsername, validateEmail, and validatePassword functions with string parameters and boolean return values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some validation functions, but make sure you have all three: validateUsername, validateEmail, and validatePassword.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation functions aren't properly defined. Create three functions named validateUsername, validateEmail, and validatePassword that each take a string parameter and return a boolean.

steps.title: Create form submission handler
steps.instruction: Define a handleSubmit function inside your ValidationForm component that validates all form fields and updates the validation errors state accordingly.
steps.hint: Create a function that prevents the default form submission, runs validation on each field, and sets errors based on validation results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSubmit function is defined that validates username and email fields and updates the errors state.
successCriteria: The handleSubmit function is defined, prevents default form submission, validates both fields using the helper functions, and sets errors state appropriately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a submission handler, but make sure it validates both username and email fields and properly updates the errors state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function is missing or incomplete. Remember to validate all form fields and update the errors state based on validation results.

steps.title: Add form container and username input
steps.instruction: In the return statement of your ValidationForm component, add a <form> element with a single <input> field for the username. Set its name, value, and onChange attributes to connect it to your form state and change handler.
steps.hint: The form should wrap the input. Use the name 'username' for the input to match your state key.
steps.expectedOutcome: A form element with a controlled username input field appears in the UI, ready for user interaction.
successCriteria: The component returns a <form> containing an <input> with name='username', value={formData.username}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the input has all three attributes: name='username', value={formData.username}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form or input isn't set up correctly. Check that you're returning a <form> with an <input> inside, and that the input's attributes match the state and handler.

steps.title: Add email and password inputs
steps.instruction: Add an email input field and a password input field to the form, below the existing username input. Both should use the same name, value, and onChange attributes as the username input, but with their respective field names.
steps.hint: Add two new <input> elements with type='email' and type='password'. Use name='email' and name='password' to match the formData keys.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form now has three input fields: username, email, and password, all wired to the formData state and handleInputChange handler.
successCriteria: Two new input elements are added: one with type='email' and name='email', and one with type='password' and name='password'. Both have value and onChange attributes correctly referencing formData and handleInputChange.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added at least one input, but make sure both email and password inputs are present with correct attributes (type, name, value, onChange).
steps.feedbackWrong: The email and password inputs are missing or incorrectly configured. Check that you've added both inputs with proper attributes.

steps.title: Add validation error display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the username input to display its validation error message from the errors state.
steps.hint:
Use the errors.username value inside a

tag. Place it right after the username input in the JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The username input will now have a paragraph below it that shows validation errors when they exist.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays errors.username below the username input.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays errors.username and is placed directly after the username input.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph for username validation errors is missing or incorrectly placed.

steps.title: Add submit button and wire form submission
steps.instruction: Add a submit button inside the form element and wire the form's onSubmit event to call the handleSubmit function.
steps.hint: Add a button with type='submit' inside the form, and add an onSubmit attribute to the form tag that calls handleSubmit.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a submit button and form submission
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <input name="task" />
  <button type="submit">Add Task</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button and the form's onSubmit event will be connected to the handleSubmit function.
successCriteria: Submit button is added inside the form
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the submit button and the onSubmit handler to the form.
steps.feedbackWrong: The submit button or form submission wiring is missing. Check that you've added a button with type='submit' and an onSubmit attribute to the form.

steps.title: Add success message display
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering inside your ValidationForm component to display a success message when there are no validation errors and the form has been submitted.
steps.hint: You can check if the errors object is empty and if form submission has occurred. Use a state variable to track submission status.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will show a success message when validation passes and the form is submitted, providing positive feedback to users.
successCriteria: A success message is conditionally rendered when there are no validation errors and the form has been submitted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check both conditions: no validation errors AND form submission status. Review the conditional logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The success message isn't displaying correctly. Ensure you're checking if the errors object is empty and tracking submission status with state.
